_what: The bar for 'could be sent to a client', cut from 658 delivered renders made by another studio and sold to its clients. Read by pipeline/scripts/deliverable_check.py.
_why_percentiles: Every image threshold here is a percentile of DELIVERED WORK, not a number the builder chose. This repo has shipped nine scorers whose thresholds were picked to be satisfiable; a percentile of work that was actually sold is the one number the builder cannot quietly move. Nothing in this file may be edited to make our frame pass — recut it from a fresh census or leave it alone.
_why_not_a_conjunction: Only 28.7% of the 658 pass all seven image rows, so an all-rows standard would reject 71% of work that was sold. Mandatory rows are correctness; scored rows are a distribution, and the pass count is the one that lands on the median of delivered work: D1 + 5 of 6 qualifies 51.4% (4/6 -> 61.7%, 6/6 -> 28.7%).
_what_the_image_rows_CANNOT_do: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT CHANGED THE PLAN. Our best frame (room_bedroom_suite_eye_ld1.png) PASSES five of the six scored image rows. Its tone, its dynamic range and its 4-32 px structure are genuinely at delivered level. A sighted judge looking at the same frame called it not sendable and named blob pillows, flat cut-out garments, white-box books, uniform plasticky roughness and an amber-monochrome cast. Of those five, the image rows can see exactly one (D10). THE IMAGE ROWS ARE A FLOOR, NOT A SUFFICIENT CONDITION. The rows that must carry the weight are the SCENE rows, and beyond them the critic ladder and the owner's eye, which stay terminal.

pool.source: _private/benchmark/candidates.json via look_bench.anchor_pool, minus the 2 reproduction-quarantined projects
pool._never_committed: the pool and the census are client imagery and stay under _private/

normalisation._why: every row except D1 is measured after resampling, so a bigger render cannot buy detail or contrast

_d7_note: D7 (>=12 loose styling objects) is reported but not scored until the shelf can supply them: CATALOG.json measures the shortfall at 8 (4 usable styling models across 29 dirs). A row that no amount of building can satisfy is a procurement decision for the owner, not a gate. It becomes mandatory the moment styling_short_by reaches 0.
_scene_rows_need_a_scene: D8 and D9 are MANDATORY, so a frame with no scene dump cannot qualify at all. That is deliberate: without them the standard is only checking tone, and tone is the half our frames already pass.

D1.why: resolution — measured on the ORIGINAL; the one row a bigger render may win

D2.why: the frame has true darks — our shadow floor sits where delivered work's does

D5.why: structure in the 4-32 px octave — two-sided, so noise cannot buy it

D6.why: share of the frame below L=26

D10.why: PROVISIONAL — the room has a colour story rather than one cast

D7.why: loose styling objects, counted from per-object ids, not from gradient blobs
